title: Qt: Restore TCP Stream switching between absolute and relative seq
description:
Commits 6bef7ffc89d63db35791003e1aeecdeb091dcb3e and
8131a4cfa9371c1981484233fdb6c84fd1e4e7e0 switched the seq and ack
numbers in the tcpheader struct from being always the absolute
sequence number to being either absolute or relative depending
on the TCP dissector relative sequence number preference.
(The ack number was changed 4 years after the seq number, which
made things particularly odd.)

When this was done, the TCP Stream tap did not adjust to this, and
so it was only able to switch between relative and absolute sequence
numbers if the TCP relative sequence number preference was off.
Restore the previous behavior. (This does restore the hint to
showing the absolute sequence number always; that could be changed
to use the current setting, though we'd need to calculate the reverse
direction offset for the ACKs.)

Also fix the relative sequence number offset computation on the TCP
Stream tap to start at 1 for non SYN packets, and to avoid using
the (always zero) ack sequence number from a reverse direction SYN.
